searches.query: trending cloud computing topics AWS Azure
searches.answer: The sources indicate that Generative AI is driving cloud spending, with hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud competing on the power and integration of their GenAI platforms. AWS is noted for its Trainium2 instances for AI training, while Azure is enhancing its Azure OpenAI Service with expanded GPT-4 support. Quantum computing in the cloud is also trending, with AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, and GCP Quantum AI providing "Quantum-as-a-Service" platforms. Additionally, serverless computing and edge computing are emerging trends, with AWS and Azure leading in multicloud interconnects and growth.

searches.answer: Kubernetes 1.20 will deprecate Docker runtime support, with the removal planned for version 1.22. Kubernetes clusters managed by Docker Desktop can still use Docker, but users will need to switch to compliant container runtimes like containerd or CRI-O to avoid breaking clusters. Kubernetes maintains release branches for the most recent three minor releases, with newer versions receiving approximately 1 year of patch support.

results.title: Releases
results.content:
The Kubernetes project maintains release branches for the most recent three minor releases (1.37, 1.36, 1.35). Kubernetes 1.19 and newer receive approximately 1 year of patch support. Kubernetes 1.18 and older received approximately 9 months of patch support.

Kubernetes versions are expressed as x.y.z, where x is the major version, y is the minor version, and z is the patch version, following Semantic Versioning terminology.
